newsitem.title: UK: Half British car drivers exceed speed limit.
newsitem.headline: Half British car drivers exceed speed limit.

text.p: More than half of British motorists exceed the speed limit on motorways (freeways) while 70 percent exceeded the speed limit on urban roads.

The Ministry of Transport said on Thursday it tested speeds at 25 motorway sites in 1996 and found 57 percent of the 76 million cars exceeded the 70 mph (112 kph) speed limit. Nineteen percent drove faster than 80 mph.
On urban roads with a speed limit of 30 mph, 72 percent exceeded the speed limit.
But speeding by coaches and lorries on motorways has been cut sharply. Only 11 percent of articulated lorries exceeded the speed limit in 1996.

Following a series of fatal accidents, coaches are currently banned from the outside lane of motorways and new coaches have been fitted with speed-limiters. Lorries are also increasingly fitted with speed limiters and congestion has caused a slowing of lorry traffic, ministry officials said.
